title: TV Host Sarah Khalifa Fighting for Her Life After Death by Hanging Sentence
excerpt: Egyptian television host Sarah Khalifa is appealing her death sentence after her conviction in an organized drug ring, according to her attorney.
content:
Sarah Khalifa, the Egyptian television host sentenced to death for her role in an organized drug ring, is fighting for her life. 

Khalifa, who faces death by hanging, will sign appeal papers Sept. 15, her attorney Mohamed El-Gendy said, according to Euronews. She has denied any involvement in the drug operation. 

The 39-year-old was arrested April 2025 in Cairo after she was identified as the “principal financier” of a group that manufactured and trafficked synthetic narcotic drugs, prosecutors said. 

Their case rested on interviews with 20 witnesses, according to the Egyptian state-owned news outlet Ahram Online, along with “messages, photographs, videos, chemical testing, analysis of seized devices and a statement attributed to another defendant.” 

Twenty-eight people were charged, with 11 condemned to death, including Khalifa’s brother Mohamed, Euronews reported. Nine others were sentenced to life and seven were acquitted, Ahram Online reported. 

Khalifa—who has 26 million Instagram followers— screamed and wept during a Sept. 5 hearing. 

“I have never smoked a cigarette in my life,” the cosmetic clinic owner told Cairo Criminal Court in a video shared to social media. “I swear to Almighty God, with the strongest oath, that I have been wronged. 

Before imposing the death penalty, the court consulted the Grand Mufti, Egypt’s highest Islamic legal authority. 

“The ruling remains appealable and is therefore not final,” Ahram Online reported. “That qualification does not return the case to the status of an accusation.” 

What Happens Next for Sarah Khalifa? 

Khalifa now has two opportunities to fight the ruling, thanks to a 2024 change in Egyptian law, Ahram Online reported at the time. 

The law made it possible for defendants to ask the courts to reconsider their convictions in an appellate trial before taking their cases to the Egyptian Court of Cassation for a final ruling. 

“Previously, the accused faced a precarious situation during the issuance of the ruling,” cassation attorney Gaber Agha told Shorouk News, according to the outlet, “as they were only tried once before being directed to the Court of Cassation directly.”  

When Khalifa presents her case again, the appellate court can, according to Euronews, either uphold, change or overturn the conviction.

Depending on the outcome, Khalifa can then plead to the Court of Cassation—the highest court in Egypt—whose role it is to make sure the law was applied correctly, according to the Cairo52 Legal Research Institute.  

It would be Khalifa’s final stop in the judicial process.
